title: Establish the physical cause of cosmic acceleration

concept.text: Establish which physical mechanism makes the expansion of the universe accelerate. The goal is to connect the measured expansion history to a quantitatively tested explanation: for example, a cosmological constant or dark energy whose properties change over time. The supplied DESI discussion illustrates why this remains difficult: existing measurements can leave these explanations insufficiently separated.

Conceptual scope: identifying the cause requires more than finding a model that fits expansion measurements. A convincing explanation should account for several kinds of observations and make successful new predictions. Gravitational alternatives remain within the concept’s broader scope, but the supplied evidence does not assess them. Establishing that a cosmological constant describes cosmic acceleration would constrain the explanation while potentially leaving its microscopic origin unresolved.

significance.text: The immediate scientific advance would be a stronger connection between observations of cosmic expansion and the explanation governing that expansion. DESI’s use of expansion geometry to test dark-energy models provides a concrete basis for this ambition. Distinguishing a constant contribution from an evolving one would substantially narrow the possible accounts of cosmic acceleration.

Conditional significance: identifying a new physical field or demonstrating a modification of gravity could fundamentally revise cosmology and connect it more closely to fundamental physics. Those outcomes require additional theoretical and observational evidence beyond distinguishing expansion histories. Likewise, support for a cosmological constant would be consequential without necessarily explaining why it has its observed value or what produces it microscopically. The revolutionary outcome is a tested physical account; improved measurements or disagreement with a familiar model would be steps toward that outcome.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central observational barrier is obtaining measurements precise and reliable enough to discriminate competing explanations. The DESI discussion describes uncertainties that prevented a previous DR2 Lyman-alpha measurement using baryon acoustic oscillations alone from clearly separating relevant models. It also addresses the role of an assumed reference cosmology and validation, underscoring that the interpretation depends on more than statistical precision.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: the missing capability is a set of discriminating tests that connects expansion history, the growth of cosmic structure and a specified physical mechanism. This requires controlling observational and analysis errors, determining which assumptions different measurements share, and developing predictions that meaningfully separate alternatives. Measurements from different instruments or analyses cannot simply be treated as independent if they depend on common calibrations, data or theoretical assumptions.

A further conceptual barrier is the gap between detecting time variation and identifying its physical cause. Evidence that a constant dark-energy description is inadequate would not by itself identify a field or establish modified gravity. Conversely, increasingly precise agreement with a constant description would not automatically explain its microscopic origin. These distinctions define the broader challenge; the supplied DESI report does not resolve the field-level or gravitational mechanisms.

current_state.text: DESI’s July 30, 2026 discussion described existing hints of evolving dark energy and reported that its new DR2 Lyman-alpha full-shape measurements agreed with the standard cosmological model. The report discussed two possible interpretations: earlier hints might fade as measurements improve, or a more complex model might be needed. Agreement of this measurement with the standard model therefore did not settle the physical cause of cosmic acceleration or establish that all earlier hints were erroneous.

The measurements test cosmological geometry and expansion history. The supplied review identifies the report’s discussion of transverse and line-of-sight baryon acoustic oscillation measurements and the Alcock–Paczynski effect as the observational basis for discriminating models. It also distinguishes the new full-shape result from a previous DR2 Lyman-alpha analysis using baryon acoustic oscillations alone, whose uncertainties were too large to clearly distinguish the models under discussion. These are demonstrated observational capabilities with unresolved physical interpretation.

The supplied evidence establishes this interpretation as of July 30, 2026. It does not explicitly substantiate the earlier characterization as a “three-year” analysis or identify the particular data combinations responsible for the evolving-dark-energy hints. No supplied follow-up search establishes developments through November 1, 2026. The review reports access to the complete, untruncated article with no extraction issues; these limitations concern attribution and temporal coverage rather than missing article text. The supplied material also does not establish the publication or peer-review status of the underlying analyses.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a quantitatively specified explanation should jointly account for independent measurements of expansion and structure growth, distinguish meaningful alternatives under explicit assumptions, and correctly predict observations excluded from the initial fit. The tests should explain which outcomes would count against the preferred explanation. A tension with one model alone would not identify the cause.
completion_criteria.label: Quantitative explanation predicts held-out expansion and structure growth observations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: independent teams should recover the central inference using separately validated measurements and analysis methods, with shared assumptions and correlations explicitly accounted for. The conclusion should remain credible under reasonable changes in calibration, data selection and modeling choices. These are proposed criteria for a convincing result, not established standards endorsed by the supplied DESI report.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce central inference across reasonable analysis choices

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: the demonstrated claim should specify its observational range and explanatory depth. Evidence for evolving dark energy should be distinguished from identification of a particular field; evidence favoring a cosmological constant should be distinguished from an explanation of its microscopic origin. Finite observations could establish predictive success across the conditions tested and rule out specified alternatives, but could not prove literal universality or eliminate every conceivable explanation.
completion_criteria.label: Claim specifies observational range and limits of physical explanation

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AST-03, identifying the physical constituent of astronomical dark matter, shares the aim of replacing an inferred cosmological component with a physical explanation. Its target is the constituent responsible for dark-matter phenomena; AST-04 targets the cause of accelerated expansion. Progress in one can inform cosmological modeling for the other without completing both discoveries.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-07, discovering a reproducible breakdown of general relativity near black holes, overlaps through tests of gravity. Its focus is gravity in the environment of black holes, whereas AST-04 concerns cosmic acceleration. A result in either domain would require an explicit theoretical and observational connection before it could establish the explanation in the other.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-05, identifying a primordial gravitational-wave background, AST-06, mapping the cosmic dark ages and first luminous structures, and AST-12, directly detecting the cosmic neutrino background, address other stages or relics of cosmic history. Their potential overlap with AST-04 lies in constraining a common cosmological account and its assumptions. None of these discoveries alone would identify the cause of acceleration. AST-10, opening the millihertz gravitational-wave sky as an observatory, is primarily an observational capability; any contribution to AST-04 would depend on the measurements and tests it ultimately enables.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish which specific earlier analyses and data combinations produced the evolving-dark-energy hints or substantiate the three-year attribution.
Developments after July 30, 2026, including the state through November 1, 2026, remain unverified in the supplied record.
The supplied evidence does not assess gravitational alternatives or identify observations that would discriminate particular modified-gravity explanations from dark-energy models.
No specific field mechanism or microscopic explanation of a cosmological constant is established by the supplied evidence.
The publication and peer-review status of the underlying DESI analyses is not established by the supplied material.

The proposed completion criteria still require a concrete choice of competing models, measurements, acceptable systematic uncertainties and predictive tests; no numerical acceptance thresholds are supplied.

brief.title: An explanation for the universe’s accelerating expansion
possible: We could understand why the universe’s expansion keeps speeding up. A tested physical explanation would connect what astronomers see to what causes it, and correctly predict observations beyond those used to build it.
why: For cosmologists, distinguishing a constant contribution from dark energy—an explanation for accelerated expansion whose properties might change over time—would narrow the possible causes. Identifying a new physical field or a change to gravity could reshape our understanding of the universe.

sources.showed: DESI used patterns in hydrogen gas between galaxies to measure cosmic expansion more precisely. Its result moved toward ΛCDM, the standard model with constant dark energy.
sources.quote: Its uncertainty is substantially smaller, and its central value shifts toward ΛCDM.
sources.cited_for: Patterns in intergalactic gas can help distinguish competing accounts of accelerated expansion.
sources.not_established: Agreement with the standard model does not identify the physical cause of acceleration.

sources.showed: The Dark Energy Survey combined measurements of expansion and the growth of matter concentrations. It found a modest preference for changing dark energy, with results stable under the analysis changes tested.
sources.cited_for: Combining expansion and matter growth measurements brings explanations under broader observational tests.
sources.not_established: Stability within one collaboration’s analysis does not establish independent reproduction or a physical mechanism.

sources.showed: DESI combined expansion measurements with other observations and found a preference for changing dark energy. Its strength depended on which sample of exploding stars was included.
sources.cited_for: Some combinations of observations favor changing dark energy over a constant contribution.
sources.not_established: A preference among fitted descriptions does not identify what causes acceleration.

sources.showed: They tested possible departures from general relativity (GR), Einstein’s theory of gravity, using DESI and other observations. Several tests agreed with GR while retaining a preference for changing dark energy.
sources.quote:

sources.cited_for: Measurements of matter clustering can test gravity alongside explanations based on dark energy.
sources.not_established: Agreement in the tested descriptions does not exclude every alternative theory of gravity.

sources.showed: Measurements of distant supernovae, exploding stars used to estimate distances, favored accelerated expansion. The conclusion survived several checks for measurement errors and bias.
sources.quote:

sources.cited_for: Distant exploding stars provided evidence for accelerated expansion.
sources.not_established: Evidence that expansion accelerates does not establish the mechanism responsible.

shown: Astronomers can now compare explanations using both the history of expansion and the growth of concentrations of matter. DESI’s more precise hydrogen-gas result agrees with constant dark energy, while some combinations of DESI and Dark Energy Survey observations favor change over time.
missing: No physical explanation has passed independent tests of expansion and matter growth while correctly predicting observations left out of its initial fit.
Independent teams have yet to reproduce a decisive conclusion while accounting for shared data, assumptions and measurement errors.
A detected change in dark energy has yet to be connected to a specific physical mechanism.

milestones.label: An explanation predicts new expansion and matter growth observations
milestones.explanation: A quantitative explanation would have to fit independent expansion and matter growth measurements and predict observations withheld from the fit. Tests that distinguish alternatives would make it possible to challenge the explanation.

milestones.label: Independent teams recover the same conclusion
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to recover the conclusion across reasonable analysis changes, accounting for shared assumptions and data. This would establish that it survives different ways of measuring and interpreting the sky.

milestones.label: The claim states its tested range and explanatory limits
milestones.explanation: The claim would have to state which observations it explains and how deeply it explains their cause. This would distinguish evidence for changing or constant dark energy from an account of its physical origin.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether hints of changing dark energy will fade with better measurements or require a more complex explanation.
Even strong support for constant dark energy could leave its physical origin and observed value unexplained.
The competing explanations, predictive tests and acceptable measurement errors needed for a decisive result remain to be specified.

page.title: Physical origin of cosmic acceleration
page.definition: A physical theory explains why cosmic expansion accelerates at late times and predicts both the expansion history and the growth of structure, the change over time in how strongly matter clusters. Possible origins include the energy of empty space, an evolving field and a change in how gravity acts on cosmological scales. A cosmological constant describes acceleration with a uniform, constant energy density. Fitting its value leaves the origin of that density open.

goal.need: In standard cosmology, dark energy accounts for about 70% of the universe’s present energy density. An explanation would show whether acceleration reveals the gravitational effect of empty space, a new field that changes over time, or a limit of general relativity. That distinction matters for judging whether expansion can continue indefinitely. More precise distances can narrow the possibilities, but some energy and gravity models predict the same expansion history and even the same growth of matter fluctuations.

completion.title: A physical mechanism for cosmic acceleration passes independent tests of expansion and structure growth.
completion.criterion: A quantitatively specified physical theory identifies the source of cosmic acceleration and is confirmed by independent observations of both expansion history and structure growth. The observations discriminate its physical mechanism from specified competing explanations within stated assumptions. A fitted cosmological constant or a time-dependent pressure-to-energy-density ratio alone is insufficient: the physical source of that behaviour must be identified. No universal significance or model-selection threshold is assigned.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; the cited programmes define observational goals without a mechanism-identification acceptance test.
completion.basis: Searched the DETF report, Astro2020 cosmology panel, NASA Physics of the Cosmos goals, WFIRST SDT goals and Euclid mission requirements for a mechanism-identification criterion, including a discovery significance, model-selection threshold or replication rule. None defines one. This fallback follows their expansion-and-growth tests while retaining the distinction between measuring dark-energy properties and identifying their physical origin.

milestones.title: Two independent supernova searches establish accelerating cosmic expansion.
milestones.criterion: Two independent Type Ia supernova searches each infer accelerating cosmic expansion from the relation between supernova brightness and redshift.
milestones.set_by: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics citation and accompanying account of the two independent searches.
milestones.threshold_quote: for the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the Universe through observations of distant supernovae

milestones.title: Multiple observational techniques, including a structure-growth probe, jointly constrain dark energy.
milestones.criterion: A joint analysis constrains dark energy using at least two observational techniques. At least one measures a quantity sensitive to the growth of cosmic structure in galaxies or galaxy clusters.
milestones.set_by: Dark Energy Task Force, Report of the Dark Energy Task Force, Recommendation II.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least one of which is a probe sensitive to the growth of cosmological structure

milestones.title: Euclid measures dark-energy parameters with a figure of merit greater than 400.
milestones.criterion: Euclid’s combined probes yield 1/√det Cov(w₀, wₐ) > 400 for its baseline non-clustering dark-energy model. Here w(a) = w₀ + wₐ(1 − a) is the ratio of pressure to energy density, and a is the scale factor, equal to 1 today. Evaluate the covariance after marginalising over the other cosmological and nuisance parameters with a Gaussian prior on the physical baryon density Ωᵦh² of mean 0.0227 and standard deviation 0.00038.
milestones.set_by: ESA's Euclid programme, Euclid Collaboration mission overview, Section 2, equation 2 and accompanying objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: so that ${\rm FoM}>400$ for this baseline scenario.

milestones.title: Euclid measures the structure-growth index with uncertainty below 0.02 at 68% confidence.
milestones.criterion: Euclid determines the dimensionless growth index γg with uncertainty below 0.02 at 68% confidence. The index parametrises the linear growth rate as f ≈ Ωm(a)^γg, where Ωm(a) is the matter density divided by the critical density. Flat cosmology with a cosmological constant and general relativity predicts γg ≈ 0.55. This target constrains gravitational explanations without itself identifying a physical mechanism.
milestones.set_by: ESA's Euclid programme, Euclid Collaboration mission overview, Section 2, equation 3 and accompanying objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: with a precision better than 0.02 (68% confidence)

milestones.title: Expansion and growth observations distinguish specified dark-energy and modified-gravity explanations.
milestones.criterion: Compare the expansion history and growth of matter fluctuations predicted by a specified new energy component in general relativity with those predicted by a specified modification of gravity. The observations distinguish the explanations through a prediction on which they differ, under explicit assumptions about the energy component and the law of gravity.
milestones.set_by: NASA-commissioned WFIRST Science Definition Team, WFIRST-2.4: What Every Astronomer Should Know, Section 3.1, first top-level question; no numerical acceptance rule is specified.
milestones.threshold_quote: Is cosmic acceleration caused by a new energy component or by the breakdown of General Relativity (GR) on cosmological scales?

milestones.title: A Stage IV survey design projects at least ten times the Stage II dark-energy figure of merit.
milestones.criterion: For a combination of techniques from one or more Stage IV projects, the projected Dark Energy Task Force figure of merit is at least 10 times the Stage II value after accounting for likely statistical and systematic uncertainties. The figure of merit is the reciprocal of the area of the 95% confidence ellipse for w₀ and wₐ, the parameters describing the present value and time evolution of the dark-energy equation of state.
milestones.set_by: Dark Energy Task Force, Recommendation IV
milestones.threshold_quote: at least a factor of ten gain over Stage II

milestones.title: A Stage III survey design projects at least three times the Stage II dark-energy figure of merit.
milestones.criterion: For a combination of techniques from one or more Stage III projects, the projected Dark Energy Task Force figure of merit is at least 3 times the Stage II value after accounting for likely statistical and systematic uncertainties. Both values use the reciprocal of the area of the 95% confidence ellipse for w₀ and wₐ, the parameters describing the present value and time evolution of the dark-energy equation of state.
milestones.set_by: Dark Energy Task Force, Recommendation III
milestones.threshold_quote: at least a factor of three gain over Stage II

milestones.title: Observations constrain how much the dark-energy density can change over cosmic time.
milestones.criterion: Under the hypothesis that a new energy component causes acceleration, infer its density history or its equation of state w(a) from observations at different epochs. Quantify the allowed time variation and test consistency with constant density, for which w(a) = −1. State the model and the redshift interval over which the constraint applies.
milestones.set_by: Dark Energy Task Force, scientific goals in sections I and III
milestones.threshold_quote: Measure as well as possible any time evolution of the dark energy.

results.finding: The Supernova Cosmology Project inferred acceleration from 54 Type Ia supernovae in its primary fit, with 99% confidence in a positive cosmological constant after identified systematics.
results.detail: The 99% figure applies to Λ > 0. The acceleration inference comes from the fit’s location relative to the zero-deceleration line.
results.quote: P(Λ > 0) = 99%, including the identiﬁed systematic uncertainties.

results.finding: In a flat, constant-w fit to 54 Type Ia supernovae, constant dark-energy density was consistent with ΩM ≈ 0.2–0.4.
results.detail: The numerical range quoted in the prose is for matter density at w = −1. Figure 10 shows the joint constraints on w and ΩM.
results.quote:
In this simple case, a cosmological-constant equa-
tion of state can ﬁt our data if the mass density is in the range
0.2 ∼< ΩM ∼< 0.4.

results.finding: The High-Z Supernova Search Team inferred cosmic acceleration at 2.8σ with MLCS using 15 spectroscopically confirmed high-redshift and 34 nearby Type Ia supernovae.
results.detail: The main analysis excluded SN 1997ck because it lacked spectroscopic classification. The supplied arXiv v1 is marked “To Appear in the Astronomical Journal.”
results.quote:
Current acceleration
of the expansion is preferred at the 99.5% (2.8 σ) to >99.9% (3.9σ) conﬁdence level.

results.finding: Joint cosmic shear, BAO and galaxy redshift-space distortion fit (41 million KiDS source galaxies) gives dark energy w₀ = −0.74 (+0.22/−0.21).
results.detail: Table 4 gives this low-redshift constraint for the evolving equation-of-state model. The fit uses neither CMB nor supernova data. The arXiv text acknowledges an anonymous referee and gives an acceptance placeholder, but identifies no journal publication.

results.finding: The Dark Energy Survey's four-probe Stage III design projects a DETF figure of merit 3.6 times the Stage II value.
results.detail: The design anticipates about 300 million galaxies and 1,100 high-quality Type Ia supernova light curves. The forecast includes nuisance-parameter marginalization, and the proposal notes that the sizes of some systematic errors remain uncertain.
results.quote:
Our own forecast constraints for DE S are shown below in Table 1 and
correspond to an increase of a factor 3.6 in the FoM over the as sumed DETF Stage II value.

results.finding: Stage IV Large Survey Telescope, combining two probes (weak lensing and baryon acoustic oscillations), projects 11× the Stage II DETF figure of merit.
results.detail: The forecast depends on achieving lower systematic errors. The report identifies photometric-redshift accuracy and galaxy-shape measurement as important uncertainties for the ground-based design.
results.quote:
If we anticipate lower systematic errors for all techniques with
an LST, then the figure of merit of an LST for WL+BAO is 11 times better than
the nominal Stage II.

results.finding: Flat DGP fit worse than expansion-matched quintessence by Δ(−2 ln L) = 8.2 across three observational datasets. Total observational sample size unreported.
results.detail: The flat fit assumes power-law primordial perturbations. The distinguishing signal is confined to the largest angular scales, where cosmic variance is substantial. The supplied text identifies the source as arXiv v2.
results.quote:
This
leads to DGP being an even worse ﬁt than QCDM with
2 ln L(QCDM) − 2 ln L(DGP) ≃ 8.

results.finding: Dark-energy density reconstructed at five knots using CMB, seven BAO redshifts and three SN Ia compilations favors variation at 2.25–2.75σ without flux averaging.
results.detail: The authors reproduce most of the inferred density pattern by projecting BAO–CMB tension into the spline under ΛCDM. Flux averaging lowers the preference for variation to 1.78σ with DES-Dovekie.

definition = "A physical theory explains why cosmic expansion accelerates at late times and predicts both the expansion history and the growth of structure, the change over time in how strongly matter clusters. Possible origins include the energy of empty space, an evolving field and a change in how gravity acts on cosmological scales. A cosmological constant describes acceleration with a uniform, constant energy density. Fitting its value leaves the origin of that density open.". Reason: The definition omits the late-time scope and the possibility that gravity itself accounts for the acceleration.

goal.need = "In standard cosmology, dark energy accounts for about 70% of the universe\u2019s present energy density. An explanation would show whether acceleration reveals the gravitational effect of empty space, a new field that changes over time, or a limit of general relativity. That distinction matters for judging whether expansion can continue indefinitely. More precise distances can narrow the possibilities, but some energy and gravity models predict the same expansion history and even the same growth of matter fluctuations.". Reason: The survey sample size gives the scale of one measurement but leaves out what the competing explanations would mean for physics and for the future of expansion.

add statement by NASA, Roman Space Telescope programme, 2023: "Is cosmic acceleration caused by a new energy component or by the breakdown of General Relativity (GR) on cosmological scales?".
